design_note: Compute rank fusion with simple integer-scaled contributions. Two different first-place documents become a new fused ordering, and the prediction removes one list to show that fusion uses rank evidence rather than raw-score addition.

source.title: Reciprocal rank fusion
source.concept: Reciprocal rank fusion adds contributions based on each document position in each result list, allowing rankings to combine without comparing incompatible raw scores.
source.scope: Original four-document lists use constant 1 and a display scale of 12 for exact arithmetic. They are not retrieval measurements or recommended tuning.

lesson.title: Fuse ranks without pretending scores share units
lesson.intro: Two authorized current-source searches use different raw-score scales. Fuse their ranks with constant 1, then multiply every fused score by 12 so the arithmetic is visible. These lists are constructed.

data.rule: Lists: lexical A,B,C; dense B,D,A. Sum 12 / (1 + rank); absence contributes 0.

read: The numbers encode rank agreement, not factual support or calibrated relevance.
lesson.question: If the dense list contributes nothing, which document ranks first and what is its displayed score?
lesson.answer: A ranks first with 12 / (1 + 1) = 6. B receives 4, C receives 3, and D receives 0. The original fused ordering changes because B loses its dense-search contribution. Authorization, source validity and evidence support remain separate checks after this arithmetic.
lesson.takeaway: Rank fusion combines ordered evidence without equating the original retrieval scores.
lesson.assumption: Constructed unique document lists with identical access filters; one-based ranks, constant 1 and display multiplier 12. Scores are not measured quality.
